items.title: How many shards actually help, given L1's own numbers?
items.description: L1's suite takes 38 minutes serially. This models what happens as it's split across more shards, using a fixed overhead per shard (spinning up, distributing files, collecting results) alongside the real per-shard work, plus a floor set by the suite's single slowest test (L3's trade-off: you can't out-shard a 90-second test). Watch how runtime drops fast at first, then flattens well before the shard count gets large.
items.compute: const totalSerialMinutes = 38; const overheadPerShardMinutes = 0.4; const slowestTestFloorMinutes = 1.5; const workPerShard = totalSerialMinutes / params.shardCount; const runtime = Math.max(workPerShard + overheadPerShardMinutes, slowestTestFloorMinutes); return { runtimeMinutes: runtime };

items.title: How many days of an un-triaged flaky test before 'just rerun it' becomes the norm?
items.description: L1's Scenario shows a real bug hiding behind 12 rerun cycles before anyone investigated. This models the share of CI failures a team stops investigating and just reruns, as a function of how many days a known-flaky test has sat without an owner or a fix -- climbing fast at first as the habit forms, then leveling off once rerunning is fully normalized.

params.name: daysUntriaged
params.label: Days the flaky test has sat un-triaged

items.compute: const maxRerunShare = 90; const rate = 0.08; const share = maxRerunShare * (1 - Math.exp(-rate * params.daysUntriaged)); return { rerunWithoutInvestigatingPercent: share };

outputs.label: CI failures rerun without investigating first
